Consider the graph of $y=f(x)$ shown above. What are the equations of its vertical asymptotes?
question.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14227291/assets/73bbd191451c2b7769ccd2903fd0e6c9da81a11853071bbfbed9711267903b9e.png)

From the given graph, we see that as $x$ approaches $-1$ from the left, the values of $f(x)$ decrease, approaching $-\infty .$ Also, notice that as $x$ approaches $-1$ from the right, the values of $f(x)$ increase, approaching $\infty .$

We also see that as $x$ approaches $1$ from the left, the values of $f(x)$ increase, approaching $\infty .$ And, as $x$ approaches $1$ from the right, the values of $f(x)$ decrease, approaching $-\infty .$

So, we can write: 

- $f(x)\to -\infty $ as $x\to -{1}^{-}$

- $f(x)\to \infty $ as $x\to -{1}^{+}$

- $f(x)\to \infty $ as $x\to {1}^{-}$

- $f(x)\to -\infty $ as $x\to {1}^{+}$

These give us the asymptotes $x=-1$ and $x=1.$
